thread:
maya: quick question — we're planning an automated egress IP rotation for the VPC NAT fleet next Tuesday 02:00 UTC. Customers with IP allowlists will likely see connection failures. Does anyone have a current per-region egress IP snapshot and any gotchas for private endpoints/partner allowlists? cc @sam @alex

sam: we have a snapshot but it changes per NAT autoscale event. for dedicated customers we keep Elastic IPs pinned. for hosted it's ephemeral unless you use PrivateLink.

sam: quick check to see your current outbound IP (for testing):
```bash
curl -s https://ifconfig.me
```

infra-bot: snapshot generated 1769987701 — us-west-2 egress set (approx): 3.34.12.45, 3.34.12.46, 3.34.12.47; eu-west-1: 18.194.5.201, 18.194.5.202. Note: hosted API pool is larger than these examples.

alex: :eyes: two things to consider — 1) partner S3 endpoints: if partners only allow IPs, we should either (a) request they accept our region-specific DNS names or (b) migrate partner traffic over PrivateLink so IP changes don't matter. 2) DNS TTLs: if we rotate and partners are resolving cached IPs, they might keep old mappings. recommend TTL=60 for transition.

maya: thanks. for partners that only accept IP allowlists, can we produce a signed notice and a stable rotation window? also want to confirm whether rotating will change private endpoint IPs (PrivateLink) — that would be bad.

sam: private endpoints (PrivateLink) are stable — they map to ENIs inside the customer's VPC, so rotating NAT egress IPs does NOT affect PrivateLink. only outbound NAT/IGW traffic changes.

jordan: can we schedule rotation during a maintenance window and post a heads-up to affected customers + support? suggest 48h notice and include the new IP set and rollback plan. also need product ops approval.

security-bot: required: create change request (JIRA SEC-1029) with risk assessment, fallback (freeze rotation + restore previous EIPs), and test plan. include customer impact matrix and list of partners with IP-only allowlists.

maya: noted — i'll create SEC-1029 and attach the per-region CSV. one more question: do we have an automated way to notify customers who have IP-only rules?

sam: we log outbound flows to customer tenants; i can run a quick query to find distinct dst IPs per tenant and match against allowlist owners. will share a CSV by EOD.

alex: if any partner refuses DNS approach, we should offer a PrivateLink migration path (low-effort for infra, high-value for reliability). tag me for migration planning.

maya: perfect. i'll draft the customer notice, schedule the maintenance, and attach the infra CSV + rollback steps to the JIRA. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: scheduled snapshot job will run again at 1769988000 UTC and push an updated list to the JIRA ticket.

security-bot: reminder — include a redaction checklist for logs in the change request (don't leak partner IPs to public logs).

sam: got it, i'll redact sensitive columns before upload.

jordan: once JIRA is up, i'll loop in support+cs to prep canned responses.

maya: closing loop here — next steps: 1) SEC-1029 created by me, 2) infra to generate final CSV, 3) security review + redaction, 4) customer notice 48h prior. ping me if anything blocks.
